title: 12 Days in Northern California
subtitle: San Francisco, Calistoga, Mendocino & Lake Tahoe
summary: Our 12-day loop through Northern California in summer 2023: Fisherman's Wharf, an Alcatraz night tour and a bike ride over the Golden Gate, Muir Woods and Point Reyes, Calistoga wineries and a geyser, the Mendocino coast by railbike, and a canoe on Lake Tahoe.

glance.label: Bases
glance.value: San Francisco (3 nights), Calistoga (2), Mendocino (2), San Francisco (1), Lake Tahoe (3)

glance.label: Getting around
glance.value: Rental car from SFO, plus walking, a ferry and bikes in the city

glance.label: Best for
glance.value: City sights, redwoods, wine country & the coast

glance.label: Highlights
glance.value: Alcatraz at night, biking the Golden Gate Bridge, Muir Woods, Old Faithful Geyser, Skunk Train railbikes, canoeing Sand Harbor

intro: This was a big loop through Northern California: four nights on Fisherman's Wharf in San Francisco, the redwoods and the Marin coast, two nights of wine tasting in Calistoga, the wild Mendocino coast, and a few days on Lake Tahoe before heading home on the Fourth of July.

The San Francisco days were packed on foot, from Lombard Street to Chinatown, with an early dinner before the evening ferry to Alcatraz. Once we picked up the car the pace slowed down: one or two big plans a day, lots of coastline, and a good dinner at the end of it. We still ran out of time for a few things, so we've left those in as ideas for next time.

days_plan.title: Newark to San Francisco
days_plan.text: An afternoon flight across the country, a rental car at SFO, and our first night at the Argonaut Hotel on Fisherman's Wharf.

Pick up the rental car at the Hertz counter
Check in at the Argonaut Hotel on Fisherman's Wharf
A late, easy dinner near the hotel

days_plan.label: Day 2
days_plan.title: Lombard Street to Chinatown, then Alcatraz at night
days_plan.text: A full day on foot: the crooked street, chocolate, the maritime park, the sea lions on Pier 39, the Ferry Building farmers market and Chinatown. An early dinner on the wharf set us up for the evening ferry to Alcatraz.

items.text: Walk from the hotel to a coffee shop for breakfast
Walk Lombard Street, the "crookedest street in the world"
Ghirardelli Chocolate Experience at Ghirardelli Square
San Francisco Maritime National Historical Park (included with the National Park Pass)
The sea lions and the shops on Pier 39
Graze our way through the Ferry Building farmers market (Saturdays 8 AM – 2 PM) to hold us until an early dinner
Golden Gate Fortune Cookie Factory, then a walk around Chinatown
Walk to Union Square for a little shopping
Early dinner at Scoma's on Fisherman's Wharf, a 10-minute walk from the Alcatraz ferry at Pier 33
Alcatraz Night Tour ferry from Pier 33 (be there by 5:30)
Ice cream at Ben & Jerry's on the way back to the hotel

days_plan.tip: Book the Alcatraz night tour well ahead: it sells out weeks in advance, and they want you at Pier 33 25 minutes before your ferry.

days_plan.label: Day 3
days_plan.title: Muir Woods, Point Bonita & biking the Golden Gate
days_plan.text: An early start for the redwoods at Muir Woods and the Point Bonita Lighthouse, a rest at the hotel, then rental bikes out to the Golden Gate Bridge and the Palace of Fine Arts.

items.text: Leave the hotel in the rental car and pick up Starbucks on the way
Muir Woods National Monument: our parking reservation was for 8:30 (bring the printed parking pass and the National Park Pass)
A quick lunch at In-N-Out Burger
Point Bonita Lighthouse in the Marin Headlands
Back to the hotel to rest
Pick up bikes from Blazing Saddles at Pier 41 and ride out to the Golden Gate Bridge
Ride back past the Palace of Fine Arts
Dinner outside at The Buena Vista, home of the famous Irish coffee

days_plan.tip: Muir Woods parking is by reservation only, and the early slots are much quieter. Download a hiking app (and the trail map) before you go: cell service in the canyon is spotty.

days_plan.label: Day 4
days_plan.title: Point Reyes, then into wine country
days_plan.text: We checked out of the Argonaut and took the long way to Calistoga. Point Reyes was fogged in, so we went with Plan B and spent the morning on Sonoma Plaza, then an afternoon tasting at Madrigal and dinner on the main street in town.

items.text: Check out of the Argonaut, grab something to eat and drive north
Explore Point Reyes National Seashore and have lunch there
Plan B if Point Reyes is fogged in: Sonoma Plaza for shops and lunch, or Mission San Francisco de Solano (about an hour from Point Reyes)
Tasting at Madrigal Family Winery (about 1.5 hours from Point Reyes)
Check in at the Inn on Pine in Calistoga, five minutes from the winery
Walk the Calistoga shops (Copperfield's Books is open until 7 PM)
Dinner outside at Calistoga Inn & Brewery, walkable from the inn

days_plan.label: Day 5
days_plan.title: Old Faithful Geyser & two wineries
days_plan.text: Calistoga's own geyser in the morning, then an afternoon of tastings without anyone having to drive.

items.text: Old Faithful Geyser of California after breakfast (it opens at 8:30)
Tasting at Bennett Lane Winery, five minutes away on the free Calistoga Shuttle
Tasting at Tank Garage Winery, a short walk from the inn
Dinner at Evangeline, walkable from the inn

days_plan.tip: The Calistoga Shuttle is free and picks you up door to door around town. Call ahead to book a pickup so tasting days don't need a designated driver.

days_plan.label: Day 6
days_plan.title: The winding road to Mendocino
days_plan.text: We checked out of the Inn on Pine and took the long, windy drive through Anderson Valley to the coast and the Brewery Gulch Inn.

items.text: Check out of the Inn on Pine and drive toward the coast
Lunch at Mosswood Market in Boonville
Coffee in Mendocino village
Check in at the Brewery Gulch Inn
A walk at Big River Beach
Stock up at the grocery store in town
Dinner and the evening wine hour at the Brewery Gulch Inn

days_plan.tip: Route 128 through Anderson Valley is curvy for the last stretch to the coast. Anyone who gets carsick should take something before Boonville.

days_plan.label: Day 7
days_plan.title: Skunk Train railbikes, Glass Beach & the headlands
days_plan.text: A day up and down the coast: pedal-powered railbikes through the redwoods out of Fort Bragg, Glass Beach and Laguna Point, then the Mendocino Headlands with the drone.

items.text: Breakfast at the Brewery Gulch Inn
Drive about 20 minutes to Fort Bragg and check in for the Skunk Train railbike tour
Skunk Train Railbike Tour along the old logging line
The model train museum
Coffee and a walk along Fort Bragg's Main Street
Glass Beach, with sea glass smoothed by decades of waves
Laguna Point in MacKerricher State Park, a short boardwalk to the harbor seals
Mendocino Headlands State Park, where Tony flew the drone over the bluffs
Back to the Brewery Gulch Inn for dinner

days_plan.tip: The railbikes are electric-assisted, so there's no real pedaling effort. Check in on time: the tour leaves right on schedule.

days_plan.label: Day 8
days_plan.title: Russian Gulch & the coast road south
days_plan.text: One last coastal hike, then the long drive back down Highway 1 to San Francisco for a night in the city.

items.text: Breakfast at the Brewery Gulch Inn
Russian Gulch State Park: the Headlands Trail to the sea cave and the Devil's Punch Bowl
Check out and drive south on Highway 1
Stops along the way: Salt Point State Park, Jenner, or Bodega Bay if the drive runs long
Something to eat on the road
Dinner in San Francisco: Boa or ramen

days_plan.label: Day 9
days_plan.title: Over the mountains to Lake Tahoe
days_plan.text: We drove east from San Francisco to South Lake Tahoe and checked in at Marriott's Timber Lodge, right in Heavenly Village.

items.text: Drive about 3.5 hours from San Francisco to South Lake Tahoe
Check in at Marriott's Timber Lodge in Heavenly Village

days_plan.label: Day 10
days_plan.title: A free day at the lake
days_plan.text: No plans on purpose: time by the water and around Heavenly Village.

days_plan.label: Day 11
days_plan.title: Canoeing at Sand Harbor
days_plan.text: An early start to beat the crowds at Sand Harbor on the Nevada shore, with its clear water and granite boulders, and a canoe out on the lake. We also hiked up to an overlook high above the lake for the view.

items.text: Leave the hotel and drive about 35 minutes to Sand Harbor (the lot opens at 7 AM)
Clearly Tahoe three-person clear-bottom canoe (get there by 7:30)
Italian dinner at Izabella, walkable from the hotel

days_plan.tip: Sand Harbor's parking lot fills up very early on summer holiday weekends. Arrive when it opens or you may be turned away.

days_plan.label: Day 12
days_plan.title: Back to San Francisco and home
days_plan.text: We checked out of the Timber Lodge and drove back to San Francisco on the Fourth of July.

tips.title: Bring the National Park Pass
tips.text: It covered the San Francisco Maritime National Historical Park and Muir Woods entry. Muir Woods still needs a separate parking reservation, printed or on your phone.

tips.title: Eat early on Alcatraz night
tips.text: The night tour ferry leaves around 6 PM. A 4 PM dinner at Scoma's, a short walk from Pier 33, meant we weren't starving on the island.

tips.title: Don't overpack the city days
tips.text: We planned more than we could do in San Francisco. Cable cars, the Painted Ladies, Golden Gate Park, Haight-Ashbury and the Musée Mécanique arcade all had to wait for next time. A Muni day pass or Clipper card makes the cable cars easy if you do get to them.

tips.title: Let the shuttle drive in Calistoga
tips.text: The free Calistoga Shuttle does door-to-door pickups around town, which makes a two-winery afternoon easy. Call ahead to book it.
